bib.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch), ch. 7: Fine-tuning to follow instructions

question: How do you instruction fine-tune a pretrained GPT-2 model on instruction-response pairs and evaluate it with an LLM judge?
contributions: Worked implementation of supervised instruction fine-tuning: Alpaca-style formatting, custom collate with -100 masking, fine-tuning GPT-2 medium, LLM-judged evaluation with Llama 3 8B via Ollama.

method.summary: Instruction-fine-tunes pretrained GPT-2 medium (355M) on a 1,100-pair instruction dataset using the Alpaca prompt style and a custom collate function, then scores test responses with Llama 3 8B Instruct run locally in Ollama.

datasets.name: Book instruction dataset (instruction-data.json)
datasets.source: Created for the book; hosted in the rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch repo
datasets.preprocessing: Alpaca prompt template, GPT-2 BPE tokenisation (tiktoken), per-batch padding with 50256, -100 mask on padding except first, truncation to 1024

training.objective: next-token cross entropy over full formatted sequence (instruction and response), padding masked with -100
training.steps: inferred: about 230+ steps (log shows Ep 2 Step 000230)
training.wall_clock: 0.87 minutes (A100); 0.86 min table; 1.83 min L4; 15.78 min M3 MacBook Air CPU

inference.decoding: book generate function; greedy (no temperature or top-k set)
inference.max_tokens: 256 new tokens for test responses (35 for the first check)
inference.samples: 1 response per test item; single judge run
inference.prompting: Alpaca-style prompt; judge prompt: Given the input `...` and correct output `...`, score the model response `...` on a scale from 0 to 100, where 100 is the best score. Respond with the integer number only.

metrics.name: Mean LLM-judge score
metrics.definition: Llama 3 8B rates each response 0-100 against the reference output; mean over test items

eval.protocol: Single run on 110 held-out test items; no significance test; author suggests repeating and averaging.

prompts.text: Given the input `{format_input(entry)}` and correct output `{entry['output']}`, score the model response `{entry[json_key]}` on a scale from 0 to 100, where 100 is the best score. Respond with the integer number only.

results.claim: The instruction dataset has 1,100 instruction-response pairs, created for the book.
Split is 85% train, 10% test, 5% validation, giving 935 / 55 / 110 examples.
results.setup: Sequential slicing (no shuffle) of the 1,100 entries.

results.claim: The 124M GPT-2 is judged too small for satisfactory instruction fine-tuning, so the 355M GPT-2 medium is used.
Fine-tuning for 2 epochs with AdamW (lr 0.00005, weight decay 0.1), batch size 8, takes about 0.87 minutes on an A100.
Initial (pre-fine-tuning) training loss on 5 batches is 3.826.
After 2 epochs train loss reaches 0.300 and val loss 0.657 at step 230.
The fine-tuned GPT-2 medium averages 50.32 on the 110-example test set, scored 0-100 by Llama 3 8B Instruct.
results.setup: Ollama llama3 8B, temperature 0, seed 123, num_ctx 2048; prompt gives input, reference output and model response; single run.
results.note: Text says 'above 50'; Ollama not fully deterministic across OS.

results.claim: Reference points under the same method: Llama 3 8B base scores 58.51 and Llama 3 8B instruct 82.6 on the test set.
results.setup: Same judge methodology; no fine-tuning (base) vs general instruction dataset (instruct).
results.quote: achieves an average score of 58.51 on the test set
results.note: Instruct figure 82.6. The base model outscores the book's fine-tuned GPT-2; the judge scores are not normalized.

results.claim: Researchers are divided on masking instruction tokens; Shi et al. 2024 found not masking helps; the chapter does not mask.
results.source: Shi et al. 2024, Instruction Tuning With Loss Over Instructions (arXiv 2405.14394)
results.setup: Chapter trains loss over instruction and response tokens, masks only padding.

limits: Judge is an 8B local model, not GPT-4; Ollama is not fully deterministic, single run, no repeat averaging reported.
Test set is the book's own 110 examples; scores not comparable to public benchmarks.
No ablation of model size, masking, prompt style or epochs; these are left as exercises.
Preference fine-tuning (DPO) is only pointed to in the repo, not covered; no RLHF or reward model.
Only 2 epochs; the author says a third may overfit, not tested.
Split is sequential, not shuffled, and no seed variation.
practices: Format entries with a prompt template (Alpaca style used; Phi-3 style shown as alternative) (7.2).
Pad per batch with a custom collate function, to the longest sequence in the batch rather than the dataset (7.3).
Build targets by shifting inputs one position and mask padding with -100 but keep one end-of-text token so the model learns to stop (7.3).
Optionally mask instruction tokens so loss covers only the response; evidence is mixed (7.3).
Truncate to the model context length (allowed_max_length=1024) (7.4).
Use a model with enough capacity: 355M rather than 124M (7.5).
Evaluate by combining benchmarks (MMLU), human preference (LMSYS arena) and LLM-judged conversational benchmarks (AlpacaEval); here an LLM judge on a custom test set (7.7).
Repeat LLM-judge evaluation several times and average because Ollama is non-deterministic (7.8).
Preference fine-tuning is an optional step after instruction fine-tuning (7.9.1).

terms.definition: Also known as supervised instruction fine-tuning: training a pretrained model on a dataset of explicit input-output pairs to follow instructions.
The format used to arrange instruction, input and response, e.g. Alpaca or Phi-3.
Ability to engage in human-like communication by understanding context, nuance, and intent.
PyTorch cross_entropy ignores targets labelled -100 by default.

lineage.note: LLM-as-judge approach is inspired by it.
